I know I’m an immigrant, so maybe there’s no help for people like me — I get it. But sometimes it’s really hard to accept: I’m here alone with my ten-year-old child, and if something happens to me, no one will step in.
Today my head was killing me. I called the GP, they said: “Sorry, no appointments — call tomorrow.” I told them: “My headache is really severe, I’m vomiting, I feel awful right now!” — and they said: “Go to the pharmacy, they’ll help.” So I went, got some pills — but they don’t work straight away. I took six — still hurting, I could barely walk to the pharmacy.
I’m just hoping it eases up, because tomorrow I have work, I need to take my kid to school — so many things I won’t manage if it stays like this. To get properly checked out, I realise: I’ll only get real help back home, not here.

I need help now, not tomorrow. But I’m scared — what if it doesn’t get better?
